title: On Talking with the stranger for an hour
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：talk　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 talk 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the clerk ① talked with the stranger for an hour without a word of thanks, and every applicant in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the clerk ② talks with the stranger for an hour at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ talk with the stranger for an hour at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ talked with the stranger for an hour before — a line in the file for May 1974 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Talking with the stranger for an hour without a word of thanks, the clerk said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ talk about nothing but the weather at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Talk about nothing but the weather at once and never mention it again.

By 1987 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the file, and a new applicant from the next office ⑧ talks about nothing but the weather without a word of thanks every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ talked with the stranger for an hour again when nobody else would.

⑩ To talk with the stranger for an hour, my mother said in 1992, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody talks with the stranger for an hour at once again and somebody must talk with the stranger for an hour without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 谈话（一般过去式 talked with the stranger for an hour：1980 年书记员头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 谈话（一般现在 talks with the stranger for an hour：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 谈话（不定式 to talk with the stranger for an hour：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 谈话（过去完成时 had talked with the stranger for an hour：1974 年五月的卷宗上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 谈话（动名词 talking with the stranger for an hour 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 谈论（talk about nothing but the weather：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去谈论除了天气再没谈别的）
G. v. 谈论（talk about nothing but the weather：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 谈话（后段两处：新来的申请人照例 talks about nothing but the weather，而母亲又一次 talked with the stranger for an hour）

answers.why: talk 意为“谈话”，1980 年书记员不图一句谢谈话与那位生人谈了一个钟头，那是办事处里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 talked。
talk 意为“谈话”，自那以后书记员二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 talks。
talk 意为“谈话”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯谈话与那位生人谈了一个钟头”，此处为不定式 to talk with the stranger for an hour。
talk 意为“谈话”，卷宗里 五月 那行字说明早在 1987 年之前就有人谈话过，故用过去完成时 had talked。
talk 意为“谈话”，书记员说“谈话与那位生人谈了一个钟头这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 talking with the stranger for an hour 作主语。
talk 意为“谈论”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去谈论除了天气再没谈别的”，should ever 之后用原形 talk about nothing but the weather。
talk 意为“谈论”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻谈论除了天气再没谈别的（talk about nothing but the weather at once），以后再也不要提起。
talk 意为“谈话”，新来的申请人每个月份都照例谈论除了天气再没谈别的，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 talks。
talk 意为“谈话”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢谈话与那位生人谈了一个钟头，用一般过去式 talked 叙述。
talk 意为“谈话”，结尾那句是母亲 1992 年的话：要谈话与那位生人谈了一个钟头，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和办事处记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 talk 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the clerk talked with the stranger for an hour without a word of thanks, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the clerk talks with the stranger for an hour at once whenever the office asks.
Talking with the stranger for an hour without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever talk about nothing but the weather at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new applicant from the next office talks about nothing but the weather without a word of thanks every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother talked with the stranger for an hour again, and the office remembered that half.
